conversations.title: Larkspur renewal: discovery call
turns: Thanks for making time, Priya. I would like to use this call to understand where the second year landed for you before we talk about renewal.
Sure. Overall it has gone well. The mis-pick rate is down and the shift leads actually use the handoff screens now.
That is great to hear. Do you remember where the mis-pick rate started in January?
It was close to six percent. We wanted to cut it in half by the end of the year.
It was 5.8 in January and 3.4 in September, so you are most of the way there.
Right. Jun, can you confirm the September number from the warehouse side?
Yes, I have it as 3.4 percent, and Boise has not even started yet.
Let us talk about Boise and Spokane. How many people will work in the two new centres?
About one hundred and twenty on the floor across the three shifts.
Do you want them on the same handoff templates as the existing sites?
Ideally yes. Can you send me a proposal for the expansion by the end of next week?
Yes, I will send the expansion proposal to you and Tomás by Friday of next week.
Good. One thing you should know: procurement asked another vendor for a quote.
Thank you for telling me. Do you know which vendor, or what they quoted?
Quill Analytics. I think it was thirty-one dollars a seat, but Tomás has the details.
Understood. What matters most to you in that comparison, price or the handoff workflow?
The workflow, honestly. But I have to justify any difference to finance.
That is fair. I will put together a total cost comparison, not just the seat price.
That would help a lot. What is the deadline to change the contract again?
It is sixty days before the thirtieth of November, so the first of October.
Then we are already close. Let us meet again on the second of October once Tomás has reviewed it.
I will hold that time and send the comparison before then.

conversations.title: Larkspur renewal: negotiation
turns: Thanks for joining. Tomás is here with me, so we can go through the numbers.
Good to have you both. I sent the comparison on Monday. Did you get a chance to read it?
I did. Your seat price is higher than Quill, and I need to understand why that is justified.
Their thirty-one dollars needs a three-year commitment, and offline use and migration cost extra. Over three years the gap narrows considerably.
What would the migration cost us, in your estimate?
Your own pilot estimate was ten weeks of rollout across three shifts, plus retraining. We would not want you to carry that.
What are you offering on the new sites?
A twelve percent volume discount on the one hundred and twenty new seats, which brings that line to about fifty-three thousand two hundred dollars a year.
A one-time fee of four thousand two hundred dollars for the two sites.
What is the total for the renewal if we take everything, including the Audit Pack?
Let me add the lines from the quote so we are exact.
Is the price increase capped? Last year we were told seven percent.
Yes, the terms cap any increase at seven percent a year, and your current seats are not changing price.
We are not comfortable with a three-year term.
We are not asking for one. A one-year renewal with the same notice window works for us.
Then I will take the proposal to finance. I need a revised quote with the Audit Pack priced separately.
I will send the revised quote with the Audit Pack as its own line by Wednesday.
Good. Priya, are you happy with the offline reliability as it stands?
Yes. The Cedarline issue last week was not a Brightwater problem, but I would like the follow-up in writing.
We will send you a written incident summary and the changes we are making by Thursday.

conversations.title: Product Designer interview: Elena Voss
turns: Welcome, Elena, and thank you for the take-home. I would like to start with how you approached the offline part of the exercise.
Thanks. I started with the twenty minutes offline, because that is where the supervisor is most likely to lose trust.
What did you decide to show the outgoing supervisor while the tablet was offline?
A clear saved on this device state on every note, and a quiet banner, not an alert, so they keep working.
How did you handle two supervisors editing the same task after reconnecting?
I showed both versions side by side and let the incoming supervisor choose, with the outgoing note kept in the history.
Tell me about a project that did not work at first. What changed?
At Harborview the dispatcher console was too dense. Dispatch time got worse for two weeks until we cut the default columns from twenty to eight.
What did you learn from that?
To test with real dispatchers on a real shift before launch, not in a meeting room.
How do you work with engineers when they say a design is too costly?
I ask which part is costly, and offer a smaller version first. In the driver app we shipped the sync states in two releases.
What are your accessibility practices for gloves and glare?
Large touch targets, forty-eight pixel minimum, high contrast, and no gestures that need precision.
How did you measure the nineteen percent improvement in dispatch time?
We compared median dispatch time for four weeks before and after, per dispatcher, to avoid mix effects.
Do you have questions for us?
What is the equity component, and how does the learning budget work?
The base range is one forty-eight to one seventy-six, with equity, and a twenty-five hundred dollar learning budget each year.
That fits my expectations. When can I expect to hear next steps?
I will confirm the panel interview date with you by the end of this week.

conversations.title: Q4 planning sync
turns: Let us start with where Q3 landed. Revenue was eleven point eight million, up twenty-two percent on last year.
And retention at one seventeen. The Business plan is now sixty-one percent of new bookings.
The constraint is the enterprise cycle, which went from ninety-four days to one hundred and eighteen.
Our target for Q4 is one hundred. Can we get there without more headcount in sales?
I think we need one more solutions engineer. Procurement reviews are what slow us down.
Noted. Let us come back to hiring after the margin discussion.
Gross margin was seventy-eight, down two points because of offline sync hosting costs.
Do we protect seventy-eight in Q4 or accept a dip while we optimise?
I would hold seventy-eight, and I will bring a hosting cost plan to the next meeting.
Agreed. Can you own that plan and report by the sixteenth of October?
Yes, I will have it by the sixteenth.
On 3.0, we release on the twentieth of October. The status page is due on the thirty-first.
Both depend on the platform team. Is there a conflict?
There is. If Cedarline keeps breaking, the status page slips.
Who owns the partner service levels?
Nobody yet. I suggest the VP Engineering with support from customer success.
Then I will assign the integration service levels to engineering, with an update by the end of the month.
Should we hire the second designer before 3.0 ships?
The hiring plan stays at two senior designers by the fifteenth of December. We will review in November.
Last item: the Audit Pack on the fifteenth of November. Is security ready?
On track. We need legal to approve the retention wording by the first of November.

conversations.title: 3.0 launch stream: dry run
turns: Welcome everyone. Today we are launching Brightwater Flow 3.0, and I am joined by Dana Whitfield from Marlow Cold Storage.
Thanks for having me. We have been running Flow for a year and a half.
Dana, what changed first when you moved from paper handoff sheets?
Arguments stopped. Everything handed over was on the record, so nobody debated what was said.
Marlow cut handoff errors by forty-one percent in ninety days. What drove that?
Templates for each dock, and tablets that work offline. Shift leads review the weekly report on Mondays.
Let me ask the chat. Maya asks: how long does setup take for a new site?
For us it was about two weeks. Before Flow, we estimated six.
Another question from chat: does 3.0 cost more?
That one is for you, not me.
No. Team stays at twenty-four dollars a seat and Business at forty-two. The Audit Pack is an add-on.
How does offline mode handle conflicts?
It shows both versions and asks who is right. It does not silently overwrite.
Ninety-nine point nine percent monthly on paid plans.
Thank you, Dana. We will share the recording and the template pack after the stream.

conversations.title: Cedarline incident follow-up call
turns: Thank you for joining. I want to walk you through what happened on the second of October and what we are changing.
Please. First, were any orders affected?
No data was lost. About three hundred and ten status updates for Larkspur were delayed and all were replayed in order.
Up to two hours fifty-eight minutes for the longest affected workspace.
Our integration partner changed an authentication token format without notice. We deployed a workaround within about an hour of finding the cause.
Do we get service credits for that?
Partner outages are excluded from the ninety-nine point nine commitment, but we committed to notify within three hours, and we did at nine o'clock.
Three things: a fourteen-day change-notice requirement with the partner, a contract test for the token format, and a status page entry for every incident.
Can you put that in writing?
Yes, I will send a written incident summary with those commitments by Thursday.
And when does the status page go live?

conversations.title: Marlow Cold Storage: quarterly check-in
turns: Dana, thank you for the time. How are the four sites doing on handoffs this quarter?
Better than last quarter. Errors are down again and new hires are productive in three days.
What would you like to see in 3.0?
Template sharing between sites, and a way to flag a handoff as urgent.
Both are on the list. I will send you the 3.0 template preview next week.
Great. Would you be open to speaking at your launch stream?
We would love that. I will send the details and a date this week.
